**Nexo v0.4 beta** streams games on Windows with a new native capture engine. Streams stay smooth while
a game keeps your graphics card busy, and viewers hear the game without hearing the voice chat. Nexo
updates itself: look for the **Restart to update** banner.

> **Hosts:** the new engine needs the updated server. On the host, back up `server/data`, run `git pull`,
> then restart the Nexo server. With an older server, streams still work: Nexo falls back to the old
> engine after a few seconds.

## What's new

- **Native capture engine (Windows).** A small helper, `nexo-media.exe`, now captures the game, encodes
  it on your graphics card's video encoder (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel) and streams it. In testing with an
  uncapped game holding the GPU at 100%, streams held **55–60 fps** while the game had focus, and the
  game lost about 1% of its frame rate. It's the default: **Settings → App → "Capture engine"** switches
  between **Native (beta)** and **Chromium**. If the helper can't start or your PC has no hardware
  encoder, Nexo uses Chromium automatically.
- **Game audio without the voice chat.** When you share a window, **App audio** sends only that game's
  sound. When you share a screen, **System audio (without Nexo)** sends everything except Nexo, so viewers
  never hear themselves or the call. Needs Windows 10 version 2004 or newer.
- **Full-screen games in the share dialog.** A full-screen game minimizes itself when you alt-tab to Nexo.
  The share dialog now lists it anyway, with its icon and a **Minimized** badge: start sharing, switch back
  to the game, and the stream starts.
- **Hide Nexo from the stream.** When you share a screen, Nexo's own window is left out of the picture
  (on by default; it's in the share dialog).
- **"You're live" card.** While you stream, your tile shows the stream's frame rate, bitrate and encoder
  instead of a preview of your own screen.
- **Steadier streams.** If the graphics driver resets or the game changes resolution, the stream recovers
  in under a second instead of ending. Viewers see and watch it on your tile, as before.

## Known limitations

- The native engine is **Windows only**. macOS and Linux stream as before.
- The engine has been tested on NVIDIA. AMD and Intel encoders should work; if your stream fails to
  start, Nexo falls back to Chromium. Please tell us if that happens.
- Friends still on v0.3 see an extra participant named after you with `#stream` while you stream. Their
  Nexo updates itself, and the extra participant goes away.
- A game that is **uncapped** can still slow the stream on a busy GPU. Capping the game's FPS a little
  below what it reaches always helps.

## Install

Already on v0.2.0-alpha.1 or later? Nothing to do: Nexo updates itself.

New here? Download the file for your system from the **Assets** below. The installers are **not
code-signed**, so your OS will warn you the first time.

- **Windows:** run `Nexo-Setup-<version>.exe`. If SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click
  **More info → Run anyway**.
- **macOS:** open the `.dmg` and drag Nexo to **Applications**. The first time, **right-click Nexo →
  Open → Open**. If macOS says the app "is damaged", run `xattr -cr /Applications/Nexo.app` in Terminal.
  Allow Nexo in **Privacy & Security → Accessibility** for global keybinds.
- **Linux:** `chmod +x Nexo-*.AppImage && ./Nexo-*.AppImage`. On Wayland, keybinds work only while Nexo
  is focused.
